newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up on Dow, political news.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up on Dow, political news.

text.p: Manila shares closed moderately higher on Wednesday in light trade on account of political developments and the Dow piercing the 7,500 mark, traders said.
"I would tend to attribute the market's rise to Wall Street achieving a new high and the Court decision," said Bing Trinidad, sales manager at DBS Securities.
The Supreme Court rejected a petition seeking to change the Constitution, dousing hopes for a second term for President Fidel Ramos and other elected officials.
The main index ended 12.63 points higher at 2,787.74. Turnover remained light at 1.5 billion pesos.
"There isn't really any corporate development and the most major item is the Supreme Court decision," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital.
Investors dabbled mostly in penny stocks and in a few selected blue chip issues such as Ayala Land Inc and Petron Corp that propped up the main index.
Gainers outnumbered decliners 59 to 49 with 76 unchanged issues.
The market's low volume, some traders said, could be attributed to a jaded view by investors on the Asian region except for Hong Kong for the time being.

"It could be a function of Asia as a whole since the Philippines has had a lot of positive news lately. These low volumes indicate scepticism," said Luz Lorenzo, research head at Peregrine Securities.
Others said investors would rather wait for second quarter corporate earnings before venturing into the market.
DBS Securities' Trinidad said the market's barometer will likely move within the 2,700 to 2,800 range in the next few days.
On June 12, the Philippine bourse will be closed to mark the celebration of Independence Day.
